24 Hansmann et al (n 12). Much of the historical work on the history of the firm has focused on the emer-

here) is not that entity shielding is empirically prior to owner shielding -indeed, as discussed below,
Roman law provided for extensive forms of owner shielding while not allowing for entity shielding.
The claim rather is that the advent of entity shielding is of greater importance 'for the creation of
business firms as separate and distinct economic actors' (at 1336).

For a discussion on the implausi-
bility of the claim of empirical priority of entity shielding see Per Samuelsson, 'On the Evolution of
